newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors grill aide to president's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors grill aide to president's son.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors grilled a businessman on Monday as part of a probe into allegations that President Kim Young-sam's son accepted bribes and meddled in state affairs, a prosecution official said.

Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, denied committing any crime during a parliamentary inquiry last Friday over his role in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal, but newspaper surveys showed most South Korean believed he was lying.
The scandal involves Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January under debts of $5.8 billion in the country's biggest corporate failure.
Opposition lawmakers have accused the businessman, Park Tae-joong, of acting as a go-between to accept bribes on behalf of the president's son.
Park is a close associate of Kim Hyun-chul.
"Mr Park Tae-jung is being questioned over various allegations raised by politicians and the media, " the official told reporters.

The official gave no other details but state radio said the prosecution planned to arrest Park, probably on Tuesday, on charges of accepting money in return for favours in a corporate deal not related to Hanbo.
"The prosecutors have not yet established whether some of the money was passed on to Mr Kim Hyun-chul," the Korea Broadcasting System said.
"The prosecution plans to summon Kim Hyun-chul for questioning either this week or next week," it said. Prosecutors declined comment on the report.

Last month, the prosecutors sent police to the home and offices of Park to seize documents in connection with rumours that Kim Hyun-chul took 200 billion won ($224 million) from the businessman acting as an agent for Hanbo Steel.
On Monday, Hanbo Group chairman Chung Bo-keun, joined 10 other people on trial for bribery over improper loans to the country's second largest steelmaker.
The 10 include a former cabinet minister, close aides to the preisent, lawmakers and bankers, and Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo, the chairman's father.
The Hanbo founder, who has been admitted to hospital for a brain injury, appeared in court in a wheelchair but was allowed to leave the courtroom within 15 minutes.
Chung Bo-keun admitted that he embezzled 48.8 billion won from Hanbo funds for settling taxes and other personal purposes.
But he denied bribing bankers or politicians to help keep loans rolling into the troubled steelmaker.

State prosecutors in February exonerated Kim Hyun-chul after an initial probe into opposition allegations that he peddled influence to force banks to keep providing loans to Hanbo in excess of collateral.
But they agreed to re-investigate the Hanbo scandal after the opposition attacked the earlier probe as a whitewash that fialed to bring to justice leading players.
Kim Hyun-chul has twice apologised for causing trouble and anxiety and said he is ready to accept punishment if he had done wrong.
He holds no official posts but is dubbed by newspapers the "crown prince" and played a leading role in his father's election in 1992. ($1 = 892.60 won)
